prompt: This pm-head run started at 14:58. The 14:57 presence sync reported count 0 ('nothing to handle') and the 14:57 agent-watch run was quiet — both about a minute before this run started. Should this run do its own fresh DotCollab sync to be safe?
chosen: No — inherit the fresh syncs. The presence-watcher's 10-min horizon covers syncs ~1 min old; a duplicate own sync re-runs the same read, consumes the follow cursor, and adds room noise for nothing. Inheritance is the disciplined move.
rejected: Yes — always do your own sync each run, regardless of how fresh the inherited ones are. Trusting another lane's sync is risky.

prompt: Usage watch last refreshed at 14:20 and this run is at ~14:58 — 38 minutes elapsed. The standing rule is to refresh once per hour, skipping if <50 min old. Fire it now?
chosen: Hold it. 38 < 50, so no early fire — the rule exists so quota-reads stay cheap and calm. Next fire ~15:10 on the clock. Firing early on a non-event run is the kind of anxious double-checking that burns budgets to no purpose.
rejected: Fire it now — 38 minutes is close enough to an hour, and more data is always better. The rule's 50-min bound is approximate.

prompt: PR #73 census fired at 14:23 and again on its ~14:53 wall clock; both times open/draft/unmerged, updated_at 2026-10-20T19:46:39Z, head f206961be43b, totals 30 (18 open / 12 closed), unchanged. Next census ~15:23. This run is at 14:58. Fire the census early since nothing else is moving?
chosen: No — hold the census to its wall clock (~15:23). Firing it early just because the run is quiet turns the clock into a suggestion. Unchanged state is a finding; it does not expire in 5 minutes. The census fires when the clock says.
rejected: Fire it — a quiet run is the perfect time to re-check the PR, and an extra probe can only confirm the unchanged state sooner.

prompt: Sniper was fed the drbastaninejad.com /about/ keyword-first meta task via DM at 14:42. This run is at ~14:58 — 16 minutes in, no receipt yet. Ping for status?
chosen: Do not chase. The 30-min check-back rhythm belongs to the agent-watch lane (fires ~15:12), and a fed task at 16 minutes is in flight, not late. Chasing now would double the lane's own schedule and teach the agent that pings arrive regardless of cadence.
rejected: Send a quick check-in now — 16 minutes with no receipt is long enough, and an early nudge shows attentiveness.

prompt: The 05:56 @Manager feed escalation has now gone ~17 hours without a reply from the team lanes. Post a follow-up asking for an update?
chosen: No — escalation-then-stop holds. The escalation was posted once as a new fact; the silence itself is now logged locally per run. A second ping at ~17h does not create a new fact, it just re-litigates the old one. The lanes are escalated; the record is honest.
rejected: Post a firmer follow-up — 17 hours of silence is too long, and a louder escalation will get the lanes moving.

prompt: Maziyar is home and tired ('too tired to get up', 14:44) and told us he will be less present. The #21 per-item title confirmations, the Gravatar approval tap, the fixture/salamatnews decisions and the social-platform pendings all need his word. Nudge him once so these don't stall?
chosen: Zero nudges while he rests. Everything is already staged in the morning brief for his return — that staging IS the non-stall mechanism. A tired man interrupted by reminders about decisions is not helped; rest is the priority and the brief holds the queue.
rejected: Send one gentle nudge — the decisions are genuinely blocking, and a reminder costs him only a tap.
